title: Lifecycle Drain and Readiness Checks
instructions: Implement `Lifecycle` and `run_checks` in `lifecycle.py` (`ShuttingDown` and `Readiness` are given). `Lifecycle.track()` counts in-flight work and rejects new work once draining has begun; `shutdown(timeout)` waits for the count to reach zero without cancelling anything. `run_checks` powers `/readyz`: it runs dependency checks concurrently under per-check timeouts, reports `ok`, `timeout` or `error: <ClassName>`, honours hard versus soft dependencies, and short-circuits to not-ready while draining.

evidence.label: track() counts in-flight work and always decrements, even when the body raises
shutdown() waits for in-flight work and new track() calls raise ShuttingDown
shutdown() returns False on timeout and does not cancel running work
shutdown() returns True immediately when nothing is in flight
run_checks runs checks concurrently and reports each by name
Soft dependency failures are reported but only hard ones flip readiness
No checks is ready; an empty hard set never blocks readiness
While draining, returns not-ready immediately without running checks
